fullName: Matilda of Flanders, Queen of England
fullNameCn: 佛兰德的玛蒂尔达，英格兰王后
notes: Wife of William the Conqueror. Birth year is approximate. Served as regent of Normandy during William's absences in England (c. 1066-1072); also called Maud.

deathCause.detail: Matilda died in Normandy on 2 November 1083. Standard accounts do not describe a violent or suspicious death.
deathCause.detailCn: 1083年11月2日玛蒂尔达在诺曼底去世。通行史料未记载暴力或可疑的死因。

events.label: Marriage to William, Duke of Normandy
events.labelCn: 与诺曼底公爵威廉成婚

events.label: Birth of Adeliza of Normandy
events.labelCn: 诺曼底的阿德莉扎出生

events.label: Birth of Cecilia of Normandy
events.labelCn: 诺曼底的塞西莉亚出生

events.label: Birth of Matilda of Normandy
events.labelCn: 诺曼底的玛蒂尔达出生

events.label: Birth of Constance of Normandy
events.labelCn: 诺曼底的康斯坦丝出生

events.label: Revolt against Emperor Henry IV
events.labelCn: 起兵反对皇帝亨利四世
events.note: Forced his father to abdicate on 31 December 1105.

events.label: King of Germany
events.note: Anointed and crowned on 5-6 January 1106 after his father's forced abdication; he had first been crowned co-ruler at Aachen on 6 January 1099.

events.label: Seizure of Pope Paschal II
events.labelCn: 拘押教皇帕斯卡尔二世
events.note: The pope was captured in February 1111 after the cancelled coronation of 12 February; the Treaty of Ponte Mammolo followed on 12 April 1111.

events.label: Imperial coronation
events.labelCn: 加冕为神圣罗马帝国皇帝

events.label: Marriage to Matilda of England
events.labelCn: 与英格兰的玛蒂尔达成婚
events.note: Wedding celebrations in Mainz; the engagement had been made at Utrecht at Easter 1110.

events.label: Concordat of Worms
events.note: Ended the Investiture Controversy between emperor and papacy.

events.label: Death at Utrecht
events.note: Died of disease; modern accounts often attribute it to cancer. He was the last Salian emperor; the marriage produced no surviving legitimate heirs.

deathCause.summary: Died of disease at Utrecht (commonly attributed to cancer)
deathCause.detail: Henry V died on 23 May 1125 at Utrecht. Contemporary sources record death from disease; later accounts commonly attribute it to cancer. His body was buried at Speyer. As the last Salian emperor he left no surviving legitimate heirs, and the crown passed to Lothair of Supplinburg.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在乌得勒支因病去世（常归因于癌症）
deathCause.detailCn: 1125 年 5 月 23 日，亨利五世在乌得勒支去世。时人记载为疾病所致，后世常归因于癌症。其遗体葬于施派尔。作为萨利安王朝最后一位皇帝，他没有留下存活的合法继承人，王位转由洛泰尔三世继承。

sourceNote: First husband of Empress Matilda; marriage ended after his death.
notes: Holy Roman Emperor and first husband of Empress Matilda. Birth date uncertain: probably 11 August 1081 or 1086 (sources disagree). German spelling 'Heinrich' is preserved per project convention.
fullNameCn: 神圣罗马帝国皇帝海因里希五世

deathPlace: Fontevraud Abbey, Anjou, Kingdom of France

events.label: Became Duchess of Aquitaine
events.note: Inherited Aquitaine after the death of William X.

events.label: Marriage to Louis, heir to France
events.labelCn: 与法兰西王储路易成婚

events.label: Birth of Alix of France
events.labelCn: 法兰西的阿利克斯出生

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Louis VII
events.labelCn: 与路易七世的婚姻被宣告无效

events.label: Marriage to Henry, Duke of Normandy
events.labelCn: 与诺曼底公爵亨利成婚

events.label: Birth of William IX, Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 普瓦捷伯爵威廉九世出生

events.label: Birth of Henry the Young King
Birth of Matilda of England
events.labelCn: 英格兰的玛蒂尔达出生

events.label: Birth of Geoffrey II, Duke of Brittany
events.labelCn: 布列塔尼公爵若弗鲁瓦二世出生

events.label: Released and governed for Richard I
events.labelCn: 获释并为理查一世摄政

events.label: Supported John after Richard I died
events.labelCn: 理查一世死后支持约翰

events.label: Embassy to Castile for Blanche of Castile
events.labelCn: 出使卡斯蒂利亚商议卡斯蒂利亚的布兰奇的婚事

deathCause.detail: Eleanor died at Fontevraud Abbey in 1204 at about 82 years old. Accounts treat her death as natural rather than violent or suspicious.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在丰特夫罗修道院去世
deathCause.detailCn: 1204 年埃莉诺在丰特夫罗修道院去世，享年约 82 岁。史料将其死亡视为自然死亡，而非暴力或可疑死亡。

deathPlaceCn: 法兰西王国安茹丰特夫罗修道院

events.label: Marriage to Aenor of Chatellerault
events.labelCn: 与沙泰勒罗的埃诺尔结婚
events.note: Married Aenor, daughter of Dangerose (his father's mistress) by her first husband Aimery of Chatellerault, easing the earlier strain between father and son caused by William IX setting aside Philippa for Dangerose.

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine, Duke of Gascony and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵、加斯科涅公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem IX in 1126. His son William Aigret died in 1130 at age four, around the time Aenor herself died.

events.label: Backed the antipope in the 1130 schism
events.labelCn: 在1130年教廷分裂中支持对立教宗
events.note: Initially supported antipope Anacletus II in the papal schism of 1130, against the wishes of his own bishops, until St. Bernard of Clairvaux persuaded him in 1134 to support Innocent II.

events.label: Raid into Normandy with Geoffrey of Anjou
events.labelCn: 与安茹伯爵若弗鲁瓦联合袭扰诺曼底
events.note: Raided Normandy in 1136 in alliance with Geoffrey V, Count of Anjou, whose son Henry later married Guilhem's daughter Eleanor.

events.label: Pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela
events.labelCn: 前往圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉朝圣
events.note: Joined the pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela in 1137, in keeping with his family's habit of pilgrimage; he died during the trip.

events.label: Death of Guilhem X
events.note: Died 9 April 1137 at Santiago de Compostela during the pilgrimage. Before dying he asked King Louis VI of France to protect his fifteen-year-old daughter Eleanor and find her a suitable husband; Louis accepted the guardianship and married her to his son, the future Louis VII.

sourceNote: Birth year varies: c. 1098 (EN infobox) vs 1099 (Chronicle of Saint-Maixent and this project's record); he was born in Toulouse during the brief period when his parents ruled it. Death: 9 April 1137 at Santiago de Compostela on pilgrimage; no cause recorded. The article itself carries citation-maintenance tags.
notes: Blank MVP card replaced with a full research-backed card; existing identity and the father/child links (to Guilhem IX and Eleanor of Aquitaine) preserved. His death left the 15-year-old Eleanor as heiress of Aquitaine; Louis VI took her under royal protection and her 1137 marriage to the future Louis VII brought Aquitaine into the French royal domain.

deathCause.summary: Died on pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela
deathCause.detail: Guilhem X died 9 April 1137 at Santiago de Compostela while on pilgrimage; no cause of death is recorded. His death left his fifteen-year-old daughter Eleanor as heiress of Aquitaine and led to her marriage with the future Louis VII of France.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉朝圣途中去世
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆十世于1137年4月9日在朝圣途中于圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉去世，死因未记载。他的去世使十五岁的女儿埃莉诺成为阿基坦继承人，并促成她与后来的法国国王路易七世成婚。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆十世
deathPlaceCn: 圣地亚哥-德孔波斯特拉

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem VIII, who died 25 September 1086. The Church initially considered him illegitimate because of his father's earlier divorces and the parents' consanguinity, until papal approval was obtained.

events.label: Marriage to Philippa of Toulouse
events.labelCn: 与图卢兹的菲莉帕结婚
events.note: Married Philippa of Toulouse in 1094, bringing her claim to the county of Toulouse. The alleged earlier marriage to Ermengarde of Anjou (1088) is doubtful (Ruth Harvey, 1993).

events.label: Capture of Toulouse
events.note: Captured Toulouse in 1098 with Philippa, asserting her inheritance claim, for which they were threatened with excommunication. He mortgaged Toulouse back to Bertrand of Saint-Gilles in 1101 to fund his crusade and lost it for good to Alfonso Jordan in 1122.

events.label: Crusade of 1101 - disaster at Heraclea
events.labelCn: 1101年十字军东征——赫拉克莱亚惨败
events.note: Led an army on the Crusade of 1101; it was destroyed by the Seljuk Turks under Kilij Arslan I at Heraclea in September 1101 and he reached Antioch with only six companions.

events.label: Excommunication and the Dangereuse affair
events.labelCn: 被绝罚及与丹格罗丝的感情风波
events.note: Excommunicated in early 1114 for infringing Church tax privileges, after threatening the bishop of Poitiers with a sword, and again for taking Dangereuse, wife of his vassal Aimery de Rochefoucauld; he installed her in the Maubergeonne tower at Poitiers and painted her likeness on his shield.

events.label: Reconciliation with the Church
events.note: Readmitted to the Church around 1118-1120 after concessions. His wife Philippa had retired to Fontevraud Abbey and died 28 November 1118.

events.label: Death of Guilhem IX
events.note: Died 10 February after a short illness in Poitiers. The year is debated: this project's record uses 1127, but the text of both EN and FR Wikipedia gives 10 February 1126 (their category boxes say 1127). He is remembered as the first troubadour whose work survives (11 songs), a founder of Occitan literature.

sourceNote: Death year is disputed: EN and FR Wikipedia article text give 10 February 1126, while their succession/category boxes and other references give 1127 (used here, matching the existing record). The traditional first marriage to Ermengarde of Anjou (1088) is doubtful. Birthplace not given by the sources.
notes: The earliest troubadour whose work survives (11 songs, one of dubious attribution); 'lo Trobador' was applied only in the nineteenth century, contemporaries sometimes calling him 'the Younger.' His affair with Dangereuse (Viscountess of Chatellerault) estranged him from his son, the future Guilhem X, whose own marriage in 1121 to Dangereuse's daughter Aenor healed the rift. Blank MVP card replaced with a full research-backed card; existing identity and father/child links preserved.

deathCause.summary: Died after a short illness in Poitiers
deathCause.detail: Guilhem IX died 10 February in Poitiers after a short illness. The year is disputed: 1127 (used in this project's data and many references) vs 1126 (EN and FR Wikipedia article text). He is remembered as the earliest troubadour whose works survive.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在普瓦捷患病后不久去世
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆九世于2月10日在普瓦捷患急病去世。年份有争议：本项目数据及许多参考文献作1127年，而英法维基百科正文作1126年。他以作品流传至今的最早游吟诗人著称。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆九世
第四代马奇伯爵罗杰·莫蒂默
birthPlaceCn: 威尔士蒙茅斯郡阿斯克
notes: Grandson of Lionel of Antwerp through his mother Philippa of Clarence. Proclaimed heir presumptive to Richard II in October 1385 (per Cokayne; historian R.R. Davies considers the story baseless, though his claim was openly discussed). NOTE: this roster entry is Roger Mortimer, 4th Earl of March (1374-1398), not the 1st Earl executed in 1330. His daughter Anne Mortimer's line carried the Yorkist claim to the throne.

deathCause.summary: Slain at the Battle of Kellistown, Ireland
deathCause.detail: Roger was killed on 20 July 1398 at the Battle of Kellistown, County Carlow, Ireland, while campaigning. Riding ahead of his army unattended and in Irish garb, he was killed by men who did not recognize him. Some sources give 15 August as the date.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在爱尔兰凯尔斯敦之战中阵亡
deathCause.detailCn: 罗杰于1398年7月20日在爱尔兰卡洛郡凯尔斯敦之战中阵亡：他孤身身着爱尔兰装束骑行在军队前方，被未认出他的士兵杀死。部分史料将日期记作8月15日。

events.label: Birth of Roger Mortimer at Usk
events.labelCn: 罗杰·莫蒂默在阿斯克出生
events.note: Born 11 April 1374 at Usk, Monmouthshire.

events.label: Inherited the Earldoms of March and Ulster
events.labelCn: 继承马奇与阿尔斯特伯爵领地
events.note: His father Edmund Mortimer, 3rd Earl, died 27 December 1381; the six-year-old Roger succeeded to the Earldom of March (Ulster title vested 1382).

events.label: Proclaimed heir presumptive to Richard II
events.labelCn: 被宣布为理查二世的推定继承人
events.note: G.E. Cokayne states Mortimer was proclaimed heir presumptive in October 1385; historian R.R. Davies calls the story baseless, though contemporary records show his claim was openly discussed.

events.label: Marriage to Eleanor Holland
events.note: Married on or about 7 October 1388, aged 14; Eleanor Holland is not modeled in the roster.

events.label: Knighted by Richard II
events.labelCn: 被理查二世册封为骑士
events.note: Knighted on St George's Day, 23 April 1390.

events.label: Lord Lieutenant of Ireland; campaigns against Irish chieftains
events.labelCn: 任爱尔兰总督并征讨爱尔兰酋长
events.note: First appointed Lord Lieutenant of Ireland on 24 January 1382 (aged 7, with uncle Sir Thomas Mortimer as deputy); reappointed July 1392, September 1394 and April 1397. He made little headway against the native Irish chieftains.

events.label: Death at the Battle of Kellistown
events.labelCn: 在凯尔斯敦之战中阵亡
events.note: Killed 20 July 1398 in County Carlow, Ireland; some sources give 15 August as the death date. Buried at Wigmore Abbey.

notes: Grandmother of Edward IV through Richard of York. Married secretly to Richard of Conisburgh; the Yorkist claim to the throne passed through her Mortimer descent, underpinning the Wars of the Roses. Birth year corrected from 1390 to 1388 (born 27 December 1388).

deathCause.detail: Anne died on or around 22 September 1411, shortly after the birth of her son Richard of York, at about age 22. Likely complications of childbirth, though the precise cause is not explicitly documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 安妮于1411年9月22日前后去世，即在生下儿子约克的理查之后不久，年仅约22岁。很可能死于分娩并发症，但具体原因无明确记载。

events.label: Birth of Anne Mortimer
events.note: Born 27 December 1388, eldest child of Roger Mortimer, 4th Earl of March, and Eleanor Holland; birthplace not documented.

events.label: Secret marriage to Richard of Conisburgh
events.labelCn: 与科尼斯伯勒的理查秘密成婚
events.note: Married secretly c. early 1408 (after 8 January) without her relatives' knowledge; validated by papal dispensation on 23 May 1408. Richard of Conisburgh is not modeled in the roster, so no relationship link is set.

events.label: Birth of Isabel of York
events.note: First child Isabel born 1409.

events.label: Birth of Richard of York
events.note: Son Richard, later 3rd Duke of York and father of Edward IV and Richard III, born 21 September 1411 (some sources: 22 September).

events.label: Death of Anne Mortimer
events.note: Died on or around 22 September 1411, soon after Richard's birth, aged about 22; buried at Kings Langley, Hertfordshire.

events.label: Mortimer claim passes to her son Richard
events.labelCn: 莫蒂默家族的继承权传于其子理查
events.note: Posthumous: her brother Edmund Mortimer, 5th Earl of March, died heirless in 1425, making her son Richard of York the Yorkist claimant to the throne.

notes: Blank MVP person card; non-marital partner of Henry II and mother of William Longespee.
Blank MVP person card; named mother of Geoffrey, Archbishop of York, in Henry II illegitimate-child tradition.
Blank MVP person card; probable mother of Morgan FitzRoy.

fullName: Matilda of Scotland, Queen of England
fullNameCn: 苏格兰的玛蒂尔达，英格兰王后
deathPlaceCn: 英格兰伦敦威斯敏斯特宫
notes: Mother of Empress Matilda; christened Edith and took the regnal name Matilda at her coronation. Known as 'Good Queen Maud'. Acted as regent of England during Henry I's absences in 1104, 1107, 1108 and 1111. An attempted sainthood was never completed.

deathCause.detail: Matilda died at Westminster Palace on 1 May 1118, aged about 37-38. No violent cause is recorded; the precise illness is not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 玛蒂尔达于1118年5月1日在威斯敏斯特宫去世，享年约37至38岁。史料未记载暴力死因，具体疾病不详。

events.label: Birth of Edith (later Matilda) at Dunfermline
events.labelCn: 埃迪丝（后来的玛蒂尔达）在邓弗姆林出生
events.note: Born c. 1080 in Dunfermline, Scotland; christened Edith (Eadgyth). Exact date unknown.

events.label: Marriage to Henry I at Westminster Abbey
events.labelCn: 在威斯敏斯特教堂与亨利一世成婚
events.note: Married 11 November 1100, officiated by Archbishop Anselm; Edith took the regnal name Matilda.

events.label: Crowned Queen of England
events.note: Crowned on her wedding day, 11 November 1100.

events.label: Birth of Empress Matilda
events.note: Daughter Matilda (later Holy Roman Empress and claimant to England) born 7 February 1102.

events.label: Birth of William Adelin
events.note: Son and heir William born 5 August 1103; he drowned in the White Ship disaster of 1120.

events.label: Regent of England during Henry I's absences
events.labelCn: 在亨利一世外出期间摄政英格兰
events.note: Acted as regent of England in 1104, 1107, 1108 and 1111 while Henry campaigned in Normandy and France; head of Henry's court during his absence.

events.label: Death of Matilda of Scotland
events.labelCn: 苏格兰的玛蒂尔达去世
events.note: Died at Westminster Palace; buried in Westminster Abbey near Edward the Confessor.

events.label: Count of Poitiers
events.note: Effective start of his tenure as count of Poitiers. Ademar of Chabannes claims he was appointed in 840 and the EN succession box gives 835, but modern scholarship (following the death of Bishop Ebroin) regards 854 as most plausible.

events.label: Wounded at the Battle of Brissarthe
events.labelCn: 在布里斯萨特战役中负伤
events.note: Fighting Viking raiders at Brissarthe on 15 September 866; Robert the Strong was killed and Ramnulf was gravely wounded by an arrow.

events.label: Death of Ramnulf I
events.note: Died of his battle wounds at Poitiers about a month after Brissarthe (15 October 866 per French Wikipedia).

sourceNote: Early Ramnulfid genealogy and dates are partly uncertain: birth year 820 (FR infobox) or c. 825 (Settipani); the start of the countship is variously given as 835/840/854; the identities of his mother and wife (Adaltrude of Maine / Bilichilde) are uncertain. He was also a lay abbot of Saint-Hilaire (841-866).
notes: Founder of the House of Poitiers/Ramnulfids; son of Gerard, Count of Auvergne according to the cited genealogy. NOTE: the EN article is titled 'Ranulf I of Aquitaine' — the previously stored URL with the 'Ramnulf' spelling returns 404 and has been corrected.

deathCause.summary: Died of wounds from the Battle of Brissarthe
deathCause.detail: Fought the Vikings at Brissarthe (15 September 866) alongside Robert the Strong, who was killed; Ramnulf was wounded by an arrow and died of his wounds in Poitiers around 15 October 866.
deathCause.summaryCn: 死于布里斯萨特战役所受的箭伤
deathCause.detailCn: 866年9月15日与罗伯特·强者一同在布里斯萨特与维京人作战；罗伯特阵亡，拉姆努尔夫中箭重伤，约10月15日在普瓦捷伤重不治。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫一世

events.label: Count of Poitiers after his father's death
events.note: Succeeded his father Ramnulf I. The EN article gives 866, French Wikipedia gives 877 and its succession box 886-890 — the start date varies by source.

events.label: Styled himself King of Aquitaine
events.note: After the death of Charles the Fat in 888 he styled himself King of Aquitaine (per the Annales Fuldenses) and refused to recognize Odo as king; the claim lasted until 889 or his death. French Wikipedia instead presents him as styling himself duke (dux maximae partis Aquitaniae), so the royal title is contested.

events.label: Death of Ramnulf II
events.note: Died at Paris on 5 August 890; French Wikipedia reports he may have been poisoned ('peut-etre empoisonne'). His legitimate son Ramnulf III was short-lived, so the illegitimate Ebalus Manzer carried the line.

sourceNote: The claim to be King of Aquitaine was short-lived and contested: it rests mainly on the Annales Fuldenses, and French Wikipedia describes only a self-styled ducal title (888-890). Count-of-Poitiers start date varies (866/877/886). He took custody of the child Charles (later Charles the Simple) after 888.
notes: Son of Ramnulf I; father of the genealogical Ramnulf III branch and of the illegitimate Ebalus Manzer. His wife Ermengarde is otherwise unrecorded and even the marriage is uncertain; the identity of his mother is debated (Bilichilde of Maine, a Guilhemide princess, or another wife of Ramnulf I).

deathCause.detail: Ramnulf II died at Paris on 5 August 890. French Wikipedia suggests he may have been poisoned, but the cause is not confirmed and the EN article gives no cause of death.
deathCause.detailCn: 拉姆努尔夫二世于890年8月5日在巴黎去世。法语维基百科推测其可能被毒杀，但死因未获确认，英文维基百科未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫二世

sourceNote: Genealogical entry; dates and detailed biography are not securely established in the cited overview.
notes: Shown as a branch of Ramnulf II in the House of Poitiers genealogy, not as the direct father of Ebalus.
fullNameCn: 阿基坦的拉姆努尔夫三世

events.label: Count of Poitiers after Ramnulf II's death
events.note: As the illegitimate son of Ramnulf II he took Poitou after his father's death, but his right to rule was challenged because he was a bastard.

events.label: Aymar seizes Poitiers; Ebalus goes into exile
events.labelCn: 埃马尔夺取普瓦捷，埃布勒斯流亡
events.note: In 892 Aymar, backed by King Odo of France, overthrew Ebalus; he fled to the safety of his father's allies William the Pious and Gerald of Aurillac.

events.label: Recovered Poitiers with William the Pious
events.labelCn: 在虔诚者威廉支持下收复普瓦捷
events.note: Retook Poitiers in 902 with an army lent by the distant relative William the Pious and was formally invested as Count of Poitou by Charles the Simple; he conquered the Limousin in 904.

events.label: Fought Rollo at the Battle of Chartres
events.labelCn: 参与沙特尔之战抗击罗洛
events.note: Participated in the campaign that defeated Rollo's Vikings at Chartres in 911 (FR Wikipedia; the exact date, 20 July or 21 August 911, varies by source).

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Auvergne
events.labelCn: 成为阿基坦公爵兼奥弗涅伯爵
events.note: After the deaths of William the Younger and his brother Acfred, Ebalus inherited the duchy of Aquitaine and the counties of Berry, Auvergne and Velay (FR dates this to 927, EN to 928). He was stripped of Berry in 929, and in 932 King Raoul transferred the duchy of Aquitaine and Auvergne to Raymond Pons of Toulouse.

events.label: Death of Ebalus Manzer
events.note: Death year given as 934 in this project's data; Wikipedia gives 934/935 (infobox 935). No cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: Wikipedia identifies Ebalus as the illegitimate son of Ranulf II; the exact maternal line is not supplied ('Manzer' is a Hebrew word meaning bastard). Birth c. 870, uncertain. Titles: Count of Poitou 890-892 and 902-934; Duke of Aquitaine 927/928-932. Death year 934/935.
notes: His line leads to the later House of Poitiers dukes and Eleanor of Aquitaine. NOTE on titles: the previous record dated his countship from 927; sources show he held Poitou continuously from 902 (after an earlier 890-892 tenure), so the entry was corrected, and the Duchy of Aquitaine (927-932) added.

deathCause.detail: No cause of death is recorded for Ebalus Manzer. The year is given as 934 in this project's data; Wikipedia gives 934/935 (infobox 935).
deathCause.detailCn: 埃布勒斯·曼泽尔的死因没有记载。项目数据记作934年；维基百科记载为934/935年（信息框为935年）。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵埃布勒斯·曼泽尔

fullName: Guilhem III Towhead, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Count of Poitiers
events.note: Succeeded his father Ebalus Manzer at Poitiers. Birth year 913 per the infobox (915 in the page's succession box); born when his father was already middle-aged.

events.label: Marriage to Gerloc of Normandy
events.labelCn: 与诺曼底的热洛丝结婚
events.note: Married Gerloc (known as Adele), daughter of Rollo of Normandy, forging a Norman alliance. The c. 936 date comes from the less reliable Dudo of Saint-Quentin and is tentative. (Gerloc is not in the roster, so no spouse link is recorded.)

events.label: Repulsed Hugh the Great's invasion
events.labelCn: 击退大胡子于格的入侵
events.note: Hugh the Great, reconciled with King Louis IV, was granted the duchies of Burgundy and Aquitaine and attacked Aquitaine with royal support; William defeated them.

events.label: Defeated at the siege of Poitiers
events.note: King Lothair and Hugh the Great besieged Poitiers in August 955; the city held out, but William gave battle and was routed. After Hugh's death, Hugh Capet was named Duke of Aquitaine but never took up the fief.

events.label: Ducal title recognized at the royal court
events.labelCn: 获王室认可为阿基坦公爵
events.note: He claimed the duchy from his father's death, but the royal chancery recognized the title only around 962 (the article's lead dates the title to 959); he was also given the abbey of Saint-Hilaire-le-Grand.

events.label: Death of Guilhem III
events.note: Died 3 April 963 at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole and was buried at the Abbey of Saint-Cyprien, Poitiers; no cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: Wikipedia notes that he was called Count of the Duchy of Aquitaine or Count Palatine, but not unambiguously Duke of Aquitaine. Uncertain: birth year 913 vs 915; start of the ducal title 959 vs 962; marriage date c. 936 tentative; the filiation of his (possible) daughter Adelaide is disputed.
notes: Occitanized display name; English and French forms remain in alsoKnownAs. 'Towhead' (Tete d'etoupe) refers to the flaxen colour of his hair, not to baldness; the Chinese nickname has been corrected from 'bald head' to 'flaxen-haired' accordingly.

deathCause.summary: Died at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem III died 3 April 963 at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole and was buried at the Abbey of Saint-Cyprien in Poitiers; the sources record no cause of death.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在圣迈克桑莱科莱去世，死因不详
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆三世于963年4月3日在圣迈克桑莱科莱去世，葬于普瓦捷的圣西普里安修道院；史料未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆三世·亚麻头

fullName: Guilhem IV Fierabras, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Count of Poitiers and Duke of Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 继承普瓦捷伯爵与阿基坦公爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem III, who retired to the abbey of Saint-Cyprien in Poitiers.

events.label: Marriage to Emma of Blois
events.note: Married Emma, daughter of Theobald I of Blois and Luitgarde of Vermandois. The marriage was stormy: Emma banished his mistresses and they separated twice.

events.label: Resisted King Hugh Capet's invasion
events.labelCn: 抵御国王于格·卡佩的入侵
events.note: Refused to recognize Hugh Capet (his brother-in-law), who invaded Aquitaine; the royal army was defeated on the plain of the Loire. He also sheltered Louis, son of Charles of Lower Lorraine, the last Carolingian heir.

events.label: Death of Guilhem IV
events.note: Died 3 February 994 and was buried at Maillezais Cathedral; an alternative date of 5 February 995 also appears (from Owen). He had retired to a monastery c. 990, leaving Emma to rule Aquitaine in the name of their son William until 1004.

sourceNote: The numbering differs between the counts of Poitiers and dukes of Aquitaine. Death date disputed: 3 February 994 (EN and FR infoboxes) vs 5 February 995 (alternative). Birth year c. 937 (c. 935 per FR). The title's end year is variously given as 990 (retirement), 993 or 995 depending on the source.
notes: Occitanized display name; Fierabras means strong-armed/iron arm in the traditional epithet (the EN article glosses it as 'Proud Arm' from Fier-a-bras). His death year has been updated from 995 to 994 following the EN/FR Wikipedia infoboxes, with the 995 alternative flagged.

deathCause.detail: No cause of death is recorded for Guilhem IV. He died 3 February 994 and was buried at Maillezais Cathedral, though an alternative date of 5 February 995 appears in some works; he had retired to a monastery c. 990 with Emma as regent.
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆四世死因没有记载。他于994年2月3日去世，葬于马耶宰大教堂；部分著作记为995年2月5日。约990年他已隐退修道院，由埃玛摄政。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆四世·铁臂

fullName: Guilhem V the Great, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem IV, who had retired to a monastery; his mother Emma of Blois acted as regent in his name until 1004.

events.label: Personal rule begins
events.note: Took up personal rule when his mother's regency ended in 1004.

events.label: Defeated by Viking raiders
events.note: Suffered a defeat against Viking invaders in 1006.

events.label: Founded Maillezais Abbey
events.note: Founded Maillezais Abbey (1010) and Bourgueil Abbey, rebuilt Poitiers cathedral after a fire, and supported the Peace and Truce of God movements — the basis of his reputation for piety.

events.label: Treaty with Fulk Nerra of Anjou
events.labelCn: 与安茹的富尔克订立条约
events.note: After losing the Loudunais and Mirebalais to Fulk Nerra, a treaty negotiated by Fulbert of Chartres (1020) defined their vassal-suzerain obligations; he also ceded Confolens, Ruffec and Chabanais to William II of Angouleme.

events.label: Declined the crown of Italy
events.note: After Emperor Henry II's death, Italian nobles offered him the kingdom of Italy; he visited Italy (1024-1025) but found the situation unfavorable and renounced the crown for himself and his heirs.

events.label: Death of Guilhem V
events.note: Died at Maillezais Abbey, which he had founded and where he is buried, on the last (or second-to-last) day of January 1030; 'his reign ended in peace.' No cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: The Ramnulfid overview identifies William V as the father of William VI, Odo, William VII and William VIII branches. Uncertain: death day (30 or 31 January 1030); the death place was corrected from Poitiers to Maillezais Abbey per the EN article; the first wife's name is given as Adalemode of Limoges (not 'Sancha').
notes: Important patron of learning and culture in Aquitaine; do not collapse his four sons into a single succession chain. He received ambassadors from Emperor Henry II, Alfonso V of Leon, Canute the Great and King Robert of France, and traveled widely, 'annually visiting Rome or Spain as a pilgrim.' NOTE: the Chinese nickname 'the Great' has been corrected from 'Grand Duke' to 'the Great one'.

deathCause.summary: Died at Maillezais Abbey; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem V died at Maillezais Abbey (which he founded) on the last or second-to-last day of January 1030, 'his reign ended in peace'; no cause of death is recorded.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在马耶宰修道院去世，死因不详
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆五世于1030年1月最后一天（或倒数第二天）在他创建的马耶宰修道院去世，'统治在和平中结束'；死因没有记载。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆五世·伟大者

fullName: Guilhem VI the Fat, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Dates are incomplete in the cited overview.
notes: Eldest son of William V; count of Poitiers from 1030 to 1038.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆六世·肥胖者

fullName: Odo of Gascony, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Half-brother of William VI according to the Ramnulfid genealogy.
notes: A collateral succession branch; not the father of William VII or William VIII.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵加斯科涅的奥多

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine after Odo's death
events.labelCn: 在奥多死后继承阿基坦公爵
events.note: Succeeded his half-brother Odo of Gascony, who was killed in battle at Mauze; Guilhem VII recovered his patrimony but did not succeed in occupying Gascony. (His sister Agnes's marriage to Emperor Henry III made him the emperor's brother-in-law.)

events.label: War with Geoffroy Martel; siege of Saumur
events.labelCn: 与若弗鲁瓦·马特尔开战并围攻索米尔
events.note: His mother Agnes had remarried Geoffroy Martel, Count of Anjou, who refused to return territories taken under earlier dukes; Guilhem took up arms and besieged Geoffroy at Saumur.

events.label: Death of Guilhem VII
events.note: Died of dysentery while besieging Saumur in autumn 1058; succeeded by his younger half-brother Guilhem VIII. The two daughters sometimes attributed to him (Clementia, Agnes) are only hypothesized.

sourceNote: Also known as Peter William; half-brother of William VI and William VIII. His wife Ermesinde is of uncertain origins, and the two daughters attributed to the couple are only hypothesized. Death: autumn 1058, of dysentery at the siege of Saumur; no exact date.
notes: The direct dynastic line to Guilhem IX runs through his brother Guilhem VIII, not through Guilhem VII. Nicknamed 'the Eagle' (Aigret) or 'the Bold' (le Hardi).

deathCause.summary: Died of dysentery at the siege of Saumur
deathCause.detail: Guilhem VII died of dysentery in autumn 1058 while besieging Geoffroy Martel of Anjou at Saumur; no exact day is recorded.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在围攻索米尔时死于痢疾
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆七世于1058年秋在围攻安茹伯爵若弗鲁瓦·马特尔所在的索米尔时死于痢疾，具体日期未记载。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆七世

events.label: Duke of Gascony
events.note: Became Duke of Gascony in 1052, succeeding Bernard II Tumapaler; Gascony had come into Aquitanian orbit through his father's marriage to Prisca of Gascony.

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his brother Guilhem VII, who died at the siege of Saumur.

events.label: Divorce from Garsende of Perigord
events.labelCn: 与佩里戈尔的加森德离婚
events.note: Divorced his first wife Garsende (November 1058), reportedly for infertility; she became a nun at Saintes.

events.label: Siege of Barbastro
events.note: Co-led the allied army aiding Ramiro I of Aragon at the Siege of Barbastro (1064), the first campaign organized by the papacy (Pope Alexander II) and a precursor of the Crusades; the city fell but was lost again within a few years.

events.label: Divorce from Matoeda
events.note: Divorced his second wife Matoeda in May 1068; their daughter Agnes later married Alfonso VI of Castile.

events.label: Pilgrimage to Rome for papal recognition
events.note: Visited Rome in the early 1070s to win papal recognition for the children of his third marriage to Hildegarde of Burgundy (his cousin), since the Church had initially considered them illegitimate. (Year approximate: 1071-1074.)

events.label: Death of Guilhem VIII
events.note: Died 25 September 1086 at Chizé, aged about 61; no cause of death recorded. His daughters' marriages to Iberian kings (Alfonso VI of Castile, Peter I of Aragon) cemented Spanish alliances.

sourceNote: Born Gui-Geoffroi; younger brother of William VII and father of William IX. Birth year c. 1025; divorce dates are precise (November 1058, May 1068); death 25 September 1086 at Chizé.
notes: Occitanized display name Guilhem VIII; the direct father link to existing Guilhem IX is now represented by UUID. His third wife Hildegarde of Burgundy was his cousin, which is why the children of that marriage initially needed papal recognition.

deathCause.summary: Died at Chizé; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem VIII died 25 September 1086 at Chizé, aged about 61; no cause of death is recorded in the sources.
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆八世于1086年9月25日在希泽去世，享年约61岁；史料未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆八世

fullName: Adèle of Champagne, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后香槟的阿黛勒
sourceNote: Third wife of Louis VII and mother of Philip II Augustus.
notes: Added as Louis VII's default spouse; Eleanor of Aquitaine remains another spouse and can be selected with the spouse direction buttons. Daughter of Theobald II, Count of Champagne (birthplace Blois per Wikipedia infobox). Served as regent of France 1190-1191 with Archbishop William of the White Hands while Philip II was on the Third Crusade.

deathCause.detail: Adèle died in Paris on 4 June 1206, aged about 66; no violent cause is recorded. She was buried at Pontigny Abbey near Auxerre.
deathCause.detailCn: 阿黛勒于1206年6月4日在巴黎去世，享年约66岁；无暴力死因记载。葬于欧塞尔附近的蓬蒂尼修道院。

events.label: Marriage to Louis VII of France
events.labelCn: 与法兰西国王路易七世成婚
events.note: Married 13 November 1160, five weeks after the death of Louis's second wife Constance of Castile; the marriage sealed a peace with her father Count Theobald II.

events.label: Crowned Queen of France
events.note: Crowned queen at Orléans on the day of her wedding, 13 November 1160.

events.label: Birth of Philip II Augustus
events.labelCn: 腓力二世·奥古斯都出生
events.note: Long-awaited son of Louis VII, born 21 August 1165 at Gonesse; nicknamed 'God-given' (Dieudonné).

events.label: Regent of France during the Third Crusade
events.labelCn: 第三次十字军东征期间摄政法兰西
events.note: Appointed regent by her son Philip II, acting together with Archbishop William of the White Hands from his departure in 1190 until his return in 1191.

events.label: Death of Adèle of Champagne
events.note: Died 4 June 1206 in Paris; buried at Pontigny Abbey.

fullName: Hugh the Great, Duke of the Franks

events.label: Count of Paris and Margrave of Neustria
events.labelCn: 成为巴黎伯爵与纽斯特里亚侯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Robert I, who died at Soissons in 923; the exact dates are approximate.

events.label: Declined the Frankish crown
events.note: After Robert I's death the crown passed to his brother-in-law Rudolph instead of Hugh.

events.label: Restored Louis IV from England
events.labelCn: 迎路易四世自英格兰归国为王
events.note: Took a very active part in bringing Louis IV (d'Outremer) back from the Kingdom of England in 936.

events.label: Marriage to Hedwig of Saxony
events.labelCn: 与萨克森的哈德维希成婚
events.note: Daughter of Henry the Fowler; mother of his five children, including Hugh Capet.

events.label: Excommunicated at the Council of Ingelheim
events.labelCn: 在英格尔海姆会议上被处以绝罚
events.note: Excommunicated in absentia at the Council of Ingelheim over his conflicts with Louis IV.

events.label: Peace with Louis IV
events.note: Made peace with the king and the church.

events.label: Invested with Burgundy and Aquitaine
events.note: After Louis IV's death he backed Lothair's coronation and was invested with the two duchies; by April 956 he was master of Burgundy.

events.label: Death at Dourdan
events.note: 16 or 17 June 956; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died of natural causes at Dourdan
deathCause.detail: Hugh died at Dourdan on 16 June (some sources say 17 June) 956, at the height of his power, about two months after becoming master of Burgundy. No violent or suspicious cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 956 年 6 月 16 日（一说 17 日）大于格在杜尔当去世，时值其权力巅峰，距其成为勃艮第实际主宰仅两个月左右。史料未载暴力或可疑死因。

sourceNote: Father of Hugh Capet; son of Robert I of France and Béatrice of Vermandois.
notes: The maternal link to Béatrice opens the documented Vermandois-Carolingian descent. Duke of the Franks and the most powerful magnate of West Francia; father of Hugh Capet, founder of the Capetian dynasty.

displayNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝
fullNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝
sourceNote: Daughter of Herbert I of Vermandois and mother of Hugh the Great; wife of Robert I of France.
notes: Her descent from the Carolingian line is through her father. Married c. 890 as the second wife of Robert of Neustria (later King Robert I); ancestress of the Capetian dynasty through her son Hugh the Great. Died after 26 March 931.

deathCause.detail: Béatrice's last known attestation is 26 March 931; she died after that date, but the exact year, place and circumstances are not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 贝阿特丽丝最后一次见于记载是931年3月26日；她在此之后去世，但确切年份、地点与情形均无记载。

events.label: Birth of Béatrice of Vermandois (c. 880)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝出生（约880年）
events.note: Born c. 880; exact date and place unknown.

events.label: Marriage to Robert of Neustria
events.labelCn: 与纽斯特里亚的罗贝尔成婚
events.note: Married c. 890 as the second wife of Robert of Neustria, who later reigned as King Robert I of France (922-923).

events.label: Became Queen of the Franks
events.note: Robert was elected king in 922; Béatrice was queen consort 922-923.

events.label: Robert I killed at the Battle of Soissons
events.labelCn: 罗贝尔一世在苏瓦松之战中阵亡
events.note: Her husband was killed on 15 June 923; their son Hugh the Great was offered the crown but refused. Béatrice was left a widow.

events.label: Death of Béatrice of Vermandois (after 931)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝去世（931年之后）
events.note: Last attested 26 March 931; died after that date, exact date unknown.

displayNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的赫伯特一世
fullNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦伯爵赫伯特一世
sourceNote: Son of Pepin of Vermandois and father of Béatrice of Vermandois.
notes: Carolingian male-line descendant through Pepin of Italy. Count of Vermandois and Soissons; his dates of accession vary by source (text: before 889; infobox: 893; existing record: 896). His capture and murder of his brother Raoul in 896 may have led Baldwin II of Flanders to have him killed in 907 (speculative).

deathCause.summary: Possibly assassinated on Baldwin II's orders
deathCause.detail: Herbert died in 907. Some historians speculate that Baldwin II of Flanders had him assassinated, possibly in retaliation for Herbert's capture and murder of his own brother Raoul in 896; the accounts are uncertain, and no battle or natural cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 赫伯特于907年去世。有史家推测他是被佛兰德伯爵鲍德温二世派人暗杀的，可能与896年赫伯特俘杀亲兄弟拉乌尔一事有关；此说尚不确定，史料亦未记载战斗或自然死亡。

events.label: Birth of Herbert I (c. 848)
events.note: Born c. 848/850; exact date unknown.

events.label: Became Count of Vermandois and Soissons
events.labelCn: 成为韦尔芒杜瓦与苏瓦松伯爵
events.note: Accession date uncertain: Wikipedia text says before 889, the infobox gives 893, the existing record uses 896.

events.label: Capture and murder of his brother Raoul
events.note: Herbert captured his brother Raoul in the upper Somme valley and had him murdered rather than ransomed; some historians link this to his own later death.

events.label: Death of Herbert I
events.note: Died 907; possibly assassinated on the orders of Baldwin II of Flanders (speculative).

sourceNote: Son of Bernard of Italy and ancestor of the Vermandois branch.
notes: Often styled Pepin I of Vermandois in genealogical references. Son of Bernard of Italy and great-grandson of Charlemagne; held Vermandois, Senlis, Péronne and Saint-Quentin. NOTE: this is Pepin I, who died c. 850 (after 850 in some genealogies) — not Pepin II (d. c. 893) nor the 'after 922' figure. Death year corrected from 845 to c. 850 per Wikipedia.

deathCause.detail: Pepin died c. 850 (some genealogies say after 850). No violent or suspicious circumstances are recorded; the exact date and cause are not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 丕平约于850年去世（部分谱系记载为850年之后）。史料未记载暴力或可疑的情形，确切日期与死因均无记载。

events.label: Birth of Pepin of Vermandois (c. 815)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的丕平出生（约815年）
events.note: Born c. 815 (Wikipedia infobox: c. 817); exact date unknown.

events.label: Count of Vermandois, Senlis, Péronne and Saint-Quentin
events.labelCn: 任韦尔芒杜瓦、桑利、佩罗讷与圣康坦伯爵
events.note: Date of succession uncertain; Wikipedia notes his son Pepin II held the county from 850.

events.label: Supported Emperor Lothar after Louis the Pious's death
events.labelCn: 虔诚者路易去世后支持皇帝洛泰尔
events.note: Despite earlier allegiance to Charles the Bald, Pepin supported Emperor Lothar in the succession struggle after Louis the Pious died (840).

events.label: Death of Pepin of Vermandois
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的丕平去世
events.note: Died c. 850 (some sources: after 850); exact date unknown.

fullName: Isabella of Hainaut, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后埃诺的伊莎贝尔
notes: First wife of Philippe II Augustus. Parents (Baldwin V of Hainaut and Margaret I of Flanders) are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Isabella gave birth to twin sons on 14 March 1190 (both died within days) and died the next day, 15 March 1190, aged 19. She was buried in Notre-Dame de Paris.
deathCause.detailCn: 1190 年 3 月 14 日伊莎贝尔产下一对双胞胎儿子（数日内先后夭折），次日（3 月 15 日）去世，年仅 19 岁，葬于巴黎圣母院。

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II at Bapaume
events.labelCn: 在巴波姆与腓力二世成婚
events.note: Her dowry was the county of Artois; both bride and groom were fifteen.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of France
events.note: Crowned at Saint-Denis.

events.label: Birth of twin sons Robert and Philippe
events.labelCn: 诞下双胞胎罗伯特与菲利普
events.note: Robert died the same day and Philippe three days later; both are excluded from the roster as infants who died young.

events.label: Died in Paris following childbirth
events.note: Philippe II was away campaigning in Normandy and did not attend the funeral.

fullName: Ingeborg of Denmark, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后丹麦的英格堡
deathPlace: Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île, near Corbeil, Kingdom of France
deathPlaceCn: 法兰西王国科尔贝附近的圣让岛修道院
sourceNote: Birth year uncertain (c. 1174/75); birthplace not recorded. Death date varies across sources (1236–1238; Wikipedia infobox gives 29 July 1237). Parents (Valdemar I of Denmark and Sofia of Minsk) are not yet in the roster.
notes: Second wife of Philippe II Augustus. Married 1193, repudiated the same day; the annulment was never canonically granted, and after the interdict crisis she was restored and remained queen until Philippe's death. The estrangement is modelled in events, not as a former marriage.

deathCause.summary: Died at the Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île
deathCause.detail: Ingeborg died on 29 July 1237 (some sources give 1236 or 1238) at the Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île near Corbeil, and was buried in the church of the Order of St John in Corbeil.
deathCause.detailCn: 1237 年 7 月 29 日（有资料作 1236 或 1238 年），英格堡在科尔贝附近的圣让岛修道院去世，葬于科尔贝圣约翰骑士团教堂。

events.label: Born in Denmark
events.note: Birth year uncertain (c. 1174/75); birthplace not recorded. Daughter of Valdemar I of Denmark and Sofia of Minsk.

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II
events.note: Married at Amiens on 14 August 1193 (the infobox gives 15 August); Philippe repudiated her the very next day, but the repudiation never obtained canonical validity.

events.label: Council of Compiègne annulment attempt
events.labelCn: 贡比涅会议企图宣告婚姻无效
events.note: About three months after the wedding Philippe summoned a council at Compiègne to annul the marriage; Danish envoys carried her appeal to Rome.

events.label: Interdict on France over the repudiation
events.labelCn: 法国因休妻事件被施以禁罚
events.note: Innocent III placed France under interdict (sources give 1199 or 1200); it was lifted in September 1200 when Philippe agreed to obey the pope.

events.label: Full reconciliation with Philippe II
events.note: Philippe reconciled with Ingeborg in 1213, after Agnes of Meran's death; she remained queen until his death in 1223.

events.label: Died at Saint-Jean-de-l'Île
events.note: Died 29 July 1237 (some sources 1236 or 1238) near Corbeil.

sourceNote: Birth year and birthplace uncertain (Wikipedia gives 1175, other sources c. 1180). Parents (Berthold IV of Merania and Agnes of Rochlitz) are not yet in the roster.
notes: Third wife of Philippe II Augustus. The 1196 marriage was contracted while Ingeborg lived and was declared invalid in 1201; her children were legitimised in November 1201. She was treated as queen but never canonically queen consort. Modelled as a former marriage (broken line), following the Eleanor x Louis VII pattern.

deathCause.detail: Agnes died in July 1201 at the castle of Poissy, possibly in childbirth, and was buried in the Convent of Saint-Corentin near Mantes.
deathCause.detailCn: 1201 年 7 月，阿涅丝在普瓦西城堡去世（可能死于分娩），葬于芒特附近的圣科朗坦修道院。

events.label: Born in Merania
events.note: Birth year uncertain (c. 1175–1180); birthplace not recorded. Daughter of Berthold IV, Duke of Merania, of the House of Andechs.

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II
events.note: Married June 1196 while Philippe's second wife Ingeborg was still living; under canon law the marriage was never valid.

events.label: Birth of Philippe Hurepel
events.labelCn: 儿子菲利普·于雷佩尔出生

events.label: Died at Poissy
events.note: Died in July 1201 (some sources give 19/20 July), possibly in childbirth; her marriage had been declared invalid earlier that year.

events.label: Children legitimised by Pope Innocent III
events.labelCn: 子女获教皇英诺森三世承认为婚生
events.note: Marie and Philippe Hurepel were legitimised by papal dispensation in November 1201, after Agnes's death.

events.label: Renewed Danish invasion of England
events.labelCn: 重启对英格兰的丹麦入侵

events.label: Conquered England
events.note: Æthelred fled to Normandy and Sweyn was acknowledged as king late in 1013.

deathCause.summaryCn: 征服英格兰后突然去世
deathCause.detail: Sweyn died at Gainsborough on 3 February 1014; the cause is not securely recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 1014年2月3日，斯温在盖恩斯伯勒去世；确切死因无可靠记载。

sourceNote: King of Denmark and briefly king of England; father of Cnut.
notes: North Sea imperial background card; basic family links are limited to the roster.

events.label: Became sole king of England
events.labelCn: 成为唯一的英格兰国王

deathCause.detail: Cnut died at Shaftesbury on 12 November 1035 after ruling England, Denmark and Norway.
deathCause.detailCn: 1035年11月12日，克努特在统治英格兰、丹麦与挪威期间去世。

sourceNote: Son of Sweyn Forkbeard; ruler of the North Sea Empire.
notes: Full North Sea Empire anchor card. Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut are represented in the roster; their mothers are intentionally not both modeled.

sourceNote: Son of Cnut and Ælfgifu of Northampton; ruled England from 1037 to 1040.
notes: Basic North Sea Empire succession card; his mother is not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Harold Harefoot died in 1040 at Oxford; the cause is uncertain, with illness and murder both suggested in the sources.
deathCause.detailCn: 1040 年，野兔脚哈罗德在牛津去世，死因不明，史料中有病故与被害两种说法。

fullNameCn: 英格兰国王哈德克努特

deathCause.detail: Harthacnut died suddenly at a wedding feast in Lambeth on 8 June 1042.
deathCause.detailCn: 1042年6月8日，哈德克努特在兰贝斯的一场婚宴上突然去世。

sourceNote: Son of Cnut and Emma; king of Denmark and England, succeeded in England by Edward the Confessor.
notes: Basic North Sea Empire succession card.

sourceNote: King during the Anarchy; succeeded by Henry II under the Treaty of Wallingford.
notes: Basic main-line succession card. His parent generation is outside the current roster.

deathCause.summary: Died of stomach illness at Dover
deathCause.detail: Stephen died in 1154 at Dover, reportedly of a stomach complaint, and was succeeded by Henry II under the Treaty of Wallingford.
deathCause.detailCn: 1154 年，斯蒂芬在多佛尔因胃疾去世，依《沃灵福德条约》由亨利二世继位。

deathCause.summary: Killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field
deathCause.summaryCn: 在博斯沃思原野战役中阵亡
deathCause.detail: Richard III was killed in battle on 22 August 1485.
deathCause.detailCn: 1485年8月22日，理查三世在战斗中阵亡。

sourceNote: Younger brother of Edward IV; last Plantagenet king of England.
notes: Basic main-line succession card.

displayNameCn: 意大利的贝伦加尔一世
fullNameCn: 意大利的贝伦加尔一世
sourceNote: Margrave of Friuli of the Unruoching dynasty; not a direct Carolingian. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 845).
notes: Margrave of Friuli who became king of Italy after the deposition of Charles the Fat, and Emperor from 915. His reign was a long contest for Italy; he was assassinated in 924.

events.label: Born, of the Unruoching dynasty
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 845.

events.label: Crowned Emperor by Pope John X
events.labelCn: 由教宗若望十世加冕为皇帝

deathCause.detail: Berengar I was murdered in 924 at Verona, reportedly by one of his own followers.
deathCause.detailCn: 924 年，贝伦加尔一世在维罗纳被刺杀，据称凶手是其一名亲随。

sourceNote: Robertian; son of Robert the Strong (not in roster) and elder brother of Robert I of France. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 857).
notes: Count of Paris of the Robertian dynasty; celebrated for the defence of Paris against the Vikings, he was elected king of West Francia in 888 — the first non-Carolingian to hold it.

events.label: Born, son of Robert the Strong
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 857.

events.label: Defence of Paris against the Vikings

deathCause.summary: Died of illness at La Fère
deathCause.detail: Odo of Paris died in 898 at La Fère after a winter campaign; the cause is usually given as illness.
deathCause.detailCn: 898 年，巴黎的厄德在一次冬季战事后于拉费尔去世，通常记为因病而亡。

sourceNote: Robertian; son of Robert the Strong (not in roster) and younger brother of Odo of Paris. Father of Hugh the Great (in roster). Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 866).
notes: Younger brother of Odo of Paris; elected king of West Francia in 922 in opposition to Charles the Simple, and killed the following year at Soissons. Father of Hugh the Great.

events.label: Born, son of Robert the Strong
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 866.

events.label: Killed at the Battle of Soissons

deathCause.summary: Killed at the Battle of Soissons
deathCause.detail: Robert I was killed in 923 at the Battle of Soissons, fighting against the forces of Charles the Simple.
deathCause.detailCn: 923 年，罗贝尔一世在苏瓦松之战中与天真者查理的军队交战时阵亡。

sourceNote: Bosonid (Bivinid) duke of Burgundy; married Emma, daughter of Robert I (neither in roster). Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 890).
notes: Duke of Burgundy of the Bosonid dynasty; elected king of West Francia in 923 after Robert I's death, reigning as a transitional figure between the Carolingians and the Capetians.

events.label: Born, of the Bosonid dynasty
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 890.

deathCause.detail: Rudolph of France died in 936 at Auxerre after falling ill during a campaign in Aquitaine.
deathCause.detailCn: 936 年，法兰西的鲁道夫在阿基坦战事中染病，于欧塞尔去世。

sourceNote: Wife Adelaide of Tours and father Robert III of Worms are not yet in the roster. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 830).
notes: Founder of the Robertian line and Marquis of Neustria, the most powerful Frankish magnate of his day. Ancestor of the Capetian kings through his sons Odo and Robert I.

deathCause.detail: Robert the Strong was killed on 15 September 866 at the Battle of Brissarthe while fighting a Viking raid.
deathCause.detailCn: 866 年 9 月 15 日，强者罗贝尔在布里萨尔泰之战中抗击维京人时阵亡。

events.label: Born, of the Robertian family
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 830.

events.label: Killed at the Battle of Brissarthe

sourceNote: Father Charles, Count of Valois, is not yet in the roster.
notes: First king of the House of Valois. His succession after the last direct Capetian was disputed by Edward III of England, beginning the Hundred Years' War.

deathCause.detail: Philip VI died in 1350 at Nogent-le-Roi after a short illness.
deathCause.detailCn: 1350 年，腓力六世在诺让勒鲁瓦因病去世。

events.label: Born, son of Charles of Valois
events.labelCn: 出生，瓦卢瓦的查理之子

events.label: Became the first Valois king
events.note: Chosen after Charles IV died without a male heir.

events.label: Hundred Years' War began
events.note: Edward III of England claimed the French throne.

events.label: Battle of Crécy
events.note: A crushing defeat by Edward III's army.

sourceNote: Wife Bonne of Bohemia is not yet in the roster.
notes: King of France during the early Hundred Years' War; captured at Poitiers and ransomed by the Treaty of Brétigny. Returned to England as a hostage and died there.

deathCause.detail: John II returned to England as a hostage in 1364 and died in London that same year.
deathCause.detailCn: 1364 年，约翰二世作为人质返回英格兰，同年死于伦敦。

events.label: Captured at the Battle of Poitiers
events.note: Taken prisoner by the Black Prince.

events.label: Ransomed by the Treaty of Brétigny
Died in London as a hostage

sourceNote: Wife Jeanne de Bourbon is not yet in the roster.
notes: Called the Wise; regent during his father's captivity, he recovered much French territory from the English under Bertrand du Guesclin and founded the royal library.

deathCause.detail: Charles V died in 1380 at Beauté-sur-Marne after a long decline in health.
deathCause.detailCn: 1380 年，查理五世在博泰叙马恩因长期病弱去世。

events.label: Recovered territory under du Guesclin
events.labelCn: 在盖克兰指挥下收复失地

events.label: Founded the royal library at the Louvre
events.labelCn: 在卢浮宫设立王室图书馆

sourceNote: Wife Isabeau of Bavaria is not yet in the roster.
notes: Called the Mad; his recurring insanity led to civil war between the Armagnacs and Burgundians, and to the Treaty of Troyes that disinherited his son.

deathCause.summary: Died after a long reign of illness
deathCause.detail: Charles VI died in 1422 at Paris after years of recurring mental illness.
deathCause.detailCn: 1422 年，查理六世在巴黎去世，此前多年饱受间歇性精神疾病困扰。

events.label: Battle of Agincourt
events.note: A devastating defeat by Henry V of England.

events.label: Treaty of Troyes — disinherited his son
events.labelCn: 《特鲁瓦条约》——废黜其子继承权
events.note: Recognized Henry V as heir to the French throne.

sourceNote: Wife Marie of Anjou is not yet in the roster.
notes: Called the Victorious; with the help of Joan of Arc he was crowned at Reims and drove the English from France, ending the Hundred Years' War.

deathCause.detail: Charles VII died in 1461 at Mehun-sur-Yèvre; tradition holds he refused food in his final illness for fear of poisoning.
deathCause.detailCn: 1461 年，查理七世在默安叙耶夫尔去世；传说他临终因怕被下毒而拒食。

events.label: Claimed the throne after Charles VI's death
Relief of Orléans with Joan of Arc
events.labelCn: 在贞德相助下解奥尔良之围

events.label: End of the Hundred Years' War

sourceNote: Wife Charlotte of Savoy and son Charles VIII are not yet in the roster.
notes: Called the Universal Spider for his web of diplomacy; he defeated Charles the Bold and annexed Burgundy, greatly strengthening the French crown.

deathCause.summary: Died after a series of strokes
deathCause.detail: Louis XI died in 1483 at Plessis-lès-Tours after a series of strokes.
deathCause.detailCn: 1483 年，路易十一世在普莱西莱图尔数次中风后去世。

events.label: War of the Public Weal
events.note: Faced a league of nobles led by Charles the Bold.

events.label: Treaty of Picquigny
events.note: Ended hostilities with Edward IV of England.

events.label: Annexed Burgundy after Charles the Bold's death
events.labelCn: 查理大胆死后吞并勃艮第

sourceNote: Father Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence is not yet in the roster. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally 1223).
notes: Queen consort of Henry III of England and mother of Edward I. Her Provençal and Savoyard relatives became influential at the English court.

deathCause.detail: Eleanor of Provence died in 1291 at Amesbury Priory, where she had retired.
deathCause.detailCn: 1291 年，普罗旺斯的埃莉诺在隐退地埃姆斯伯里修道院去世。

events.label: Born in Provence
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally 1223.

events.label: Gave birth to the future Edward I
events.labelCn: 生下未来的爱德华一世

sourceNote: Father René of Anjou and son Edward of Westminster are not yet in the roster.
notes: Queen consort of Henry VI and a driving force of the Lancastrian cause in the Wars of the Roses. Her son Edward of Westminster died at Tewkesbury.

deathCause.detail: Margaret of Anjou died in 1482 at Dampierre-sur-Loire after years in exile following the Lancastrian defeat.
deathCause.detailCn: 1482 年，兰开斯特败北后流亡多年的玛格丽特在当皮埃尔去世。

events.label: Lancastrian defeat at Tewkesbury
events.labelCn: 兰开斯特在蒂克斯伯里败北
events.note: Her son Edward of Westminster was killed.

sourceNote: Father Charles VI of France is in the roster; second husband Owen Tudor is not.
notes: Daughter of Charles VI and queen consort of Henry V, mother of Henry VI. After Henry V's death she married Owen Tudor, founding the Tudor dynasty's claim.

deathCause.detail: Catherine of Valois died in 1437, shortly after childbirth, and was buried at Westminster Abbey.
deathCause.detailCn: 1437 年，凯瑟琳产后不久去世，葬于威斯敏斯特教堂。

events.label: Married Henry V after the Treaty of Troyes
events.labelCn: 依《特鲁瓦条约》嫁给亨利五世

events.label: Gave birth to the future Henry VI

sourceNote: Father William I of Hainault is not yet in the roster; sons Edward the Black Prince and John of Gaunt are in the roster.
notes: Queen consort of Edward III and mother of the Black Prince and John of Gaunt. Remembered for her gentleness and as a patron of the arts.

deathCause.detail: Philippa of Hainault died in 1369 at Windsor Castle after a long illness.
deathCause.detailCn: 1369 年，埃诺的菲利帕在温莎城堡久病后去世。

events.label: Born in Hainault
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally 1310.

events.label: Married Edward III of England
events.labelCn: 嫁给英格兰爱德华三世

sourceNote: Father Gorm the Old is not yet in the roster. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 958).
notes: King of Denmark and Norway who unified the Danes and converted them to Christianity, commemorated at the Jelling stones. Father of Sweyn Forkbeard.

deathCause.detail: Harald Bluetooth was killed in 986 during a rebellion, reportedly with the involvement of his son Sweyn Forkbeard.
deathCause.detailCn: 986 年，蓝牙哈拉尔在一场叛乱中被杀，据称其子斯温八字胡亦有参与。

events.label: Born, son of Gorm the Old
events.note: Birth year uncertain, traditionally c. 958.

fullNameCn: 北安普顿的埃尔夫吉芙
sourceNote: First wife of Cnut by Danish custom; mother of Harold Harefoot and Svein Knutsson. Birth and death years are uncertain.
notes: First wife of Cnut the Great and mother of Harold Harefoot and Svein Knutsson. Distinguished from Emma of Normandy, Cnut's church-married second wife.

events.label: Born in Northampton
events.note: Birth year uncertain.

fullNameCn: 诺曼底公爵夫人贡诺尔
sourceNote: Wife of Richard I of Normandy and mother of Richard II and Emma of Normandy. Birth and death years are approximate.
notes: Duchess consort of Normandy and mother of Richard II and of Emma, whose children included Edward the Confessor and Harthacnut.

events.label: Married Richard I of Normandy
events.labelCn: 嫁给诺曼底的理查一世

events.label: Died in Normandy
events.note: Death year approximate.

sourceNote: Son of Cnut the Great and Ælfgifu of Northampton, half-brother of Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut.
notes: Son of Cnut by Ælfgifu of Northampton; king of Norway under his father's overlordship. Died young.

events.label: Born, son of Cnut and Ælfgifu
events.labelCn: 出生，克努特与埃尔夫吉芙之子

sourceNote: Wife of Godwin and mother of Harold II, Tostig, Gyrth, and Leofwine. Birth and death years are approximate.
notes: Danish noblewoman, wife of Earl Godwin and mother of Harold II and his brothers; sister of Jarl Ulf of Denmark.

events.label: Married Earl Godwin
events.note: Marriage year approximate.

sourceNote: Second husband Hugh X of Lusignan is not yet in the roster.
notes: Queen consort of John and mother of Henry III. Her later marriage to Hugh X of Lusignan helped spark the Barons' Wars against her son.

deathCause.detail: Isabella of Angoulême died in 1246 at Fontevraud Abbey.
deathCause.detailCn: 1246 年，昂古莱姆的伊莎贝尔在丰特夫罗修道院去世。

events.label: Gave birth to the future Henry III

sourceNote: First wife of Edward I and mother of Edward II.
notes: First wife of Edward I and mother of Edward II. After her death, Edward raised the Eleanor crosses to mark her funeral procession.

deathCause.detail: Eleanor of Castile died in 1290 at Harby, Nottinghamshire, and Edward I raised the Eleanor crosses in her memory.
deathCause.detailCn: 1290 年，卡斯蒂利亚的埃莉诺在诺丁汉郡哈比去世，爱德华一世为其立埃莉诺十字架以纪念。

events.label: Married the future Edward I
events.labelCn: 嫁给未来的爱德华一世

events.label: Gave birth to the future Edward II
events.labelCn: 生下未来的爱德华二世

birthPlaceCn: 英格兰格拉夫顿里吉斯
sourceNote: Wife of Edward IV and mother of Edward V and Elizabeth of York. Birth year is uncertain (traditionally c. 1437).
notes: Queen consort of Edward IV and mother of the Princes in the Tower and of Elizabeth of York, wife of Henry VII.

deathCause.detail: Elizabeth Woodville died in 1492 at Bermondsey Abbey.
deathCause.detailCn: 1492 年，伊丽莎白·伍德维尔在伯蒙德西修道院去世。

events.label: Gave birth to Elizabeth of York

primaryTitleCn: 里士满与德比伯爵夫人
sourceNote: Mother of Henry VII by Edmund Tudor (not yet in the roster).
notes: Mother of Henry VII and a key architect of the Tudor accession through her Lancastrian Beaufort descent.

deathCause.detail: Margaret Beaufort died in 1509 at Westminster, shortly after her grandson Henry VIII's accession.
deathCause.detailCn: 1509 年，玛格丽特·博福特在威斯敏斯特去世，时值其孙亨利八世即位后不久。

events.label: Gave birth to the future Henry VII

sourceNote: First wife of Richard II.
notes: First wife of Richard II; her death was deeply mourned and helped unsettle Richard's later reign.

deathCause.detail: Anne of Bohemia died in 1394 at Sheen Palace, likely of plague.
deathCause.detailCn: 1394 年，波希米亚的安妮在希恩宫去世，据信死于瘟疫。

sourceNote: Common-law wife of Harold II. Birth and death years are approximate.
notes: Common-law wife of Harold II, remembered as the Edith who identified his body after Hastings.

events.label: Traditionally identified Harold's body after Hastings
events.labelCn: 相传黑斯廷斯之战后辨认哈罗德遗体
